newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile telecom Manquehue joins long-distance market.
newsitem.headline: Chile telecom Manquehue joins long-distance market.

text.p: Chilean telecom Telefonica Manquehue, which joined the competitive long-distance telephone market this month, expects to win a 10 percent market share by the end of 1998, said a top company official.
"We believe we will reach 10 percent within the next 18 months," Rafael Valdivieso, president of Manquehue Telecomunicaciones de Larga Distancia, told a news conference.
Valdivieso said Manquehue, which already operates local telephone services in Santiago, has invested $10 million in moving into the long distance market.

Part of the investment will be financed by funds from the sale last year of a 17 percent stake in holding company, Telefonica Manquehue, to a U.S. foreign investment fund, The Latin American Enterprise Fund. The rest of the company is owned by the Rabat family. Manquehue will be the ninth company to operate in Chile's highly competitive multi-carrier long-distance market, which was deregulated two years ago.
Valdivieso said the firm decided to make its debut now as the price war, which dominated the start-up of the service, was mostly over.
Telecom prices tumbled sharply after deregulation, but have recovered over the last year, although they are not as high as before the multi-carrier system.
